stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist wants to use the state pharmacist-prescribing pathway for hormonal contraception. Which product category is within the described statutory and protocol scope?

choices.text: Eligible hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives after required screening.
Any implanted contraceptive device selected by the pharmacist without a protocol.
Any injectable contraceptive solely because it is prescription-only.
Any Schedule II medication used for a reproductive-health indication.
Any hormonal product requested by a patient without screening.

explanation.core_reasoning: The Massachusetts pharmacist-prescribing pathway described in the current rule covers eligible hormonal contraceptive patches and self-administered oral hormonal contraceptives, with required screening and protocol compliance.

choice_analysis.A: This matches the dosage-form scope and required screening described by the Massachusetts pathway.
choice_analysis.B: The rule does not create an unrestricted pharmacist pathway for implanted devices.
choice_analysis.C: Prescription-only status alone does not place an injectable product within this specific pathway.
choice_analysis.D: Controlled-substance status does not expand the contraception protocol.
choice_analysis.E: Required screening and protocol conditions cannot be omitted simply because the patient requests the product.

related_facts: The pharmacist-prescribing authority is protocol-based and product-category specific.
The pathway is separate from collaborative drug therapy management.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not broaden a narrow pharmacist-prescribing statute into general independent prescribing authority.

reasoning_steps: Match the requested dosage form to the authorized scope
